name: Sansa, Buddhist Mountain Monasteries in Korea
description: Seven Buddhist temples tucked into the mountains of southern Korea make up this site, founded between the 7th and 9th centuries. Each is built around a madang, an open courtyard framed by a Buddha hall, a pavilion, a lecture hall and monks' dormitories. Rich with old buildings, relics and shrines, they are still active places of daily worship, not museums.
